ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$, $\angle A=68^\circ$, $\angle ACD=30^\circ$. Find: the measure of $\angle BDC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle BDC=\angle A+\angle ACD$, and $\angle A=68^\circ$, $\angle ACD=30^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle BDC=68^\circ+30^\circ=\boxed{98^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$, $\angle A=68^\circ$, and $\angle ACD=30^\circ$. Find the measure of $\angle BDC$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point D is located on side AB, and the line segment CD from C to D is drawn. Then reason: The problem states that CD bisects ∠ACB, and ∠ACD = 30°, therefore ∠DCB = 30°, so ∠ACB = 60°. Also ∠A = 68°, in triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 180° - 68° - 60° = 52°. Because D is on AB, ∠CBD = ∠CBA = 52°. In triangle BCD, ∠BDC = 180° - ∠CBD - ∠DCB = 180° - 52° - 30° = 98°.
